record.paper_title: Approximation by rational functions: Open problems.
record.context_brief: Rational approximation with infinitely many poles in E_R
record.original_question: Let E be a closed bounded subset of the complex plane whose complement is simply connected, and let G be the Green function of the complement of E with pole at infinity. For R>1, let E_R be the finite region bounded by the level curve G(z)=log R. In the classical theory discussed on the source page, if a function f is analytic on E and meromorphic in E_R with only finitely many poles, then there are rational-approximation results that parallel polynomial approximation theorems for best rational approximants R_{mn}. The open problem is to determine whether the corresponding approximation theory still holds when f is meromorphic in E_R but has infinitely many poles there instead of only finitely many poles.

evidence.page: zbMATH review text, main summary paragraph
evidence.quote: Some recent results on approximation by rational functions relate the table of rational functions (*) ... of best approximation to a given function f(z) on a closed bounded set E to approximation by polynomials, notably the case where E is a closed bounded set whose complement is simply connected and f(z) is analytic on E, meromorphic with ν poles in the finite region E_R bounded by the level locus G(z)=log R of Green’s function for the complement of E with pole at infinity. The corresponding problem where f(z) has an infinity of poles in E_R is open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a closed bounded subset of the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$ whose complement $\mathbb{C}_\infty\setminus E$ (in the Riemann sphere) is simply connected, and let $G(z)$ denote the Green function of $\mathbb{C}_\infty\setminus E$ with pole at infinity. For each $R>1$, let
$$E_R=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: G(z)<\log R\}\cup E$$
be the finite region bounded by the level curve $G(z)=\log R$. For nonnegative integers $m,n$, let $R_{mn}(f;z)$ denote a rational function of type $(m,n)$ (numerator degree at most $m$, denominator degree at most $n$) of best uniform approximation to $f$ on $E$, and consider the table $\{R_{mn}\}$ as $m,n\to\infty$.

The classical theory establishes the following: if $f$ is analytic on $E$ and meromorphic in $E_R$ with exactly $\nu$ poles in $E_R\setminus E$ (counted with multiplicity), then convergence and degree-of-approximation theorems for the rows and diagonals of the table $\{R_{mn}\}$ hold, paralleling the polynomial approximation theory of Walsh-type for analytic functions and giving rates governed by $R$ and the pole locations.

Problem: Does an analogous theory of best rational approximation $R_{mn}$ on $E$ hold when $f$ is analytic on $E$ and meromorphic in $E_R$ with infinitely many poles in $E_R\setminus E$? Specifically, formulate and prove (or disprove) convergence and degree-of-approximation theorems for $R_{mn}(f;\cdot)\to f$ in the case where the set of poles of $f$ in $E_R$ is infinite.
artifact.category_tag: Rational approximation in the complex plane
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a definitive resolution of this specific question about extending the Walsh-type best rational approximation theory on $E$ from finitely many to infinitely many poles in $E_R$. The Walsh/Gonchar theory and subsequent work (Saff, Gonchar, and others on row/diagonal convergence and the Gonchar–Walsh class) addresses related convergence and spurious-pole phenomena for meromorphic functions, but the specific classical open problem as stated could not be confirmed as resolved or formally open from the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Spurious Poles in Diagonal Rational Approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies spurious poles for diagonal and sectorial sequences of rational approximants to functions in the Gonchar–Walsh class.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on rational approximation of meromorphic functions exists but does not directly resolve the stated infinite-pole question.

status_evidence.title: Rational Approximation (arXiv:2501.00902)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys rational approximation theory including Walsh/Gonchar theory and the case of meromorphic functions with poles.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys discuss rational approximation of meromorphic functions but do not announce a resolution of the classical infinite-pole problem on E_R.
